variants.title: Payment API delays checkout
variants.context: The checkout endpoint calls a payment provider synchronously and waits on every call.
variants.constraint: The dependency is slow and thread-blocking.
variants.question: What makes request latency recover?
variants.expectedPattern: Enqueue the payment work and return quickly to the user.
wrongChoices: Move the API code into the browser

variants.title: Email sends hang the request path
variants.context: Emails are sent during signup and each request waits for SMTP completion.
variants.constraint: External email sending is slow and often unreliable.
variants.question: What should happen after the user account is created?
variants.expectedPattern: Persist a work item and process it asynchronously.

variants.title: Thumbnails generate too slowly
variants.context: Users upload photos and the app renders thumbnails inline in the request path.
variants.constraint: Thumbnail generation is slow and deferrable.
variants.question: What is the correct design?
variants.expectedPattern: Store the upload, enqueue the thumbnail job, and respond immediately.
wrongChoices: Render thumbnails in the request thread
Cache the upload in the browser
Queue thumbnails without storing the original

variants.title: Pay later crash
variants.context: A worker crashes after charging a card but before acknowledging the message.
variants.constraint: The queue may redeliver the same job.
variants.question: How do you avoid charging twice?
variants.expectedPattern: Use idempotency keys and a safe deduplication strategy.
wrongChoices: Let the request handle the charge

variants.title: Flash sale on the checkout system
variants.context: Payment, email, and order processing happen inside the request while the sale peaks.
variants.constraint: Downstream dependencies are slow and the pool is exhausting threads.
variants.question: What is the right architectural move?
variants.expectedPattern: Queue the expensive downstream tasks and make the request path short.

variants.title: Background workers back up
variants.context: The queue is growing and workers are falling behind under a sudden spike.
variants.constraint: Work is queueing faster than it can be processed.
variants.question: What should be added to prevent collapse?
variants.expectedPattern: Backpressure, retry policies, worker parallelism, and workload prioritization.

variants.title: Complex order processing
variants.context: After a user places an order, the platform calculates taxes, emits notifications, and updates a ledger.
variants.constraint: These steps do not need to complete before the user receives confirmation.
variants.question: How should the order flow be modeled?
variants.expectedPattern: Acknowledge the order quickly, then process the downstream work asynchronously.
wrongChoices: All work on the web request

variants.title: Queue message duplication
variants.context: A message is processed twice because a worker crashes before acknowledging it.
variants.question: What safety property must the job handler provide?
variants.expectedPattern: Idempotent processing so duplicate messages do not cause duplicate side effects.

variants.title: User places order but waits too long
variants.context: The order request waits for analytics, tax calculation, and three downstream APIs before returning a response.
variants.constraint: Only the order status is needed immediately.
variants.question: How do you improve user experience without losing correctness?
variants.expectedPattern: Queue non-critical follow-up work and acknowledge the order quickly.
wrongChoices: Wait for all APIs in the request

variants.title: Crashes during message processing
variants.context: A worker starts processing a message, fails mid-way, and the queue redelivers it.
variants.constraint: The side effect is not safe to repeat unless designed carefully.
variants.question: What must you design for?
variants.expectedPattern: Idempotent handlers, retry limits, and observational state.
